do we need inventoryPath check here ?
Why not? Caller can pass any `nlohmann::json` object reference

Agree with @anupama.b.r1@ibm.com
Why do we need an inventory check here? This is a utility methods to get "getUnexpandedLocationCodeForFru". If that field is there, it should return the location code else give error.
Ok. Addressed.
should we use unordered_map<string, vector<string>> once the keys are build up, search will be more efficient and constant time ?
Agreed. I have addressed this.
Done
do we need try catch block here, as each tag is checked before accessing. ?
As of today, `try catch` may not be needed here, but this is a safe programming approach we use in all our utility APIs so that they never throw exception.
Done

The description is not clear. What do you mean by "JSON object for a single FRU"?
It should clearly state that you are expecting a sub JSON which reflect a single JSON in system config JSON?
Done
This can be pulled as an independent function? Let's not keep on extending the base API. It is already almost 100 lines of code.
Done
why is Res from variable l_locationCodeRes ?
Do you mean "what is Res?" "Res = result"

+1 I did not get the objective of res in the name. 

If I read it somewhere below the code, the name in any way does not tell that it holds un-expanded location code.
It holds some location code result... what is that result?
"Res" just signifies that the variable doesn't directly contain the location code, but may also alternatively hold an error value.
Addressing this to make things simple.
How are we dealing with the error code here?
Addressed.

Can be optimized?
m_unexpandedLocCodeToInvPathMap[l_locationCodeRes.value()].emplace_back(l_inventoryPath);
Done
can we name as buildLocCodeToInvPaths() or buildLocCodeToInvPathsMapForFru ?
What's the benefit of the extra 's'? The documentation makes it clear there can be multiple inventory paths for a given location code.

the variable name says map of locationCode to inventory path, but its represent map of locationCode to inventory paths. So we follow naming convention matches with the type, should this be get updated ?

"ForFru" at the end is confusing me.
It is a map of Location code to inventory path(s) period. Any additional information is diluting the purpose here.

With For Fru comes to my mind questions like
-> Which Fru?
-> All Fru>
-> Sub Fru?
-> Parent Fru .... etc.

Lets keep it crisp and simple, close to it s purpose.... 
some thing like buildLocCodeToInvPathMap?

"For Fru" signifies that this API builds the unexpanded location code to inventory path(s) map for a given FRU represented by the input parameter. It doesn't build this map for all FRUs in the system configuration JSON.

This is following the same naming convention as `buildConfigMapsForFru` in line 132.

As we are using 's' here buildConfigMapsForFru, it sounds clear understanding of multiple maps are updated here.
why can't we follow same pattern for this api with buildLocCodeToInvPaths*()

The documentation makes that clear though. But I agree, some developers may forget to look at documentation, so updating the name with an extra `s` here.

Also, removing the "forFru" part to keep things simple.
m_unexpandedLocCodeToInvPathsMap ?
What's the benefit of the extra 's'? The documentation makes it clear there can be multiple inventory paths for a given location code.
I agree, some developers may forget to look at documentation, so updating the name with an extra s here.
Your comment is perfect, so should be the function name.
Done.
can it be named as i_subFrusJsonObj or i_subFrusJsonArray  ?
What's the justification?
we referring json object as *JsonObj irrespective of its type in the other parts for the code and Array should be used with plural naming convention, which sounds clearer ?
An array by definition means a collection of homogeneous variables. So plurality is inbuilt in the definition. Also, we have used `l_subFruJsonArray` in line 122 of config_manager.cpp earlier.
Done
